DOCTOR VISIT LESSON · DOCTOR VISIT · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Appointment — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the appointment as a plan on the calendar: the visit becomes something counted down to, not something that happens to a child.

What is this?

An appointment is the agreed time for the check-up — a day, a time and a doctor, written where the family can see it.

What does it mean?

Surprises are what make check-ups hard. A child who has crossed days off a calendar walks in already owning the visit: this was planned, and plans are safe.

What does the child need to know?

You need the appointment card, a real calendar and a crayon. Circle the day together. Every morning after, cross one more day off — a countdown any two-year-old can run.

Why this matters

The countdown does the emotional work days in advance. The morning of the visit there is nothing left to explain — the plan is simply finished, and off you go.

What it teaches

Time words (today, tomorrow, two more sleeps), anticipation managed in small doses, and the first experience of "planning" as a family skill.

Words to learn

appointmentcalendartodaytomorrowplanvisit

Say this to your child

“"Appointment! A time to visit the doctor. See — the calendar says today. We planned this! Teddy is coming too. Let’s go keep our plan."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "an appointment is a time to visit the doctor."
  2. Find the real day on the calendar and circle it together.
  3. Cross off each day as it passes — "two more sleeps!"
  4. The night before, pack with the child: teddy, the waiting-bag, socks with dinosaurs on them.
  5. In the morning: "appointment day! The plan says today."

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "appointment — a time to visit the doctor" sit over a parent and child walking along, teddy under one arm, beside a calendar marked TODAY.

Ask your child

"What day is our appointment?" "Who comes with us?" "What do we pack the night before?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might circle every day on the calendar "just in case," pack the teddy a week early, or announce "appointment day!" to the whole street.

Out in the real world

Dentists, haircuts, grandma’s birthday — every one of them lives on the same calendar. The countdown trick works at all of them.

Try it together

Calendar Countdown: a paper chain with one ring per day; each morning the child pulls one off. One ring left means appointment day. The pulling is the therapy.

Understanding check

Ask: "Where does the visit live?" (on the calendar) "What do we cross off?" (the days) "Who comes with us?" (me — and teddy)

Staying safe

An appointment is a plan, never a warning. Say the day warmly — the tone a child hears on the calendar page is the tone they bring to the clinic.

This lesson pairs with the Appointment flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Doctor Visit.
